items.issueTitle: E-0002 Edit LH004 into an article

feedback.message: Drafted articles/the-xz-backdoor.md from LH004: about 1,200 words, three headings plus Sources, one illustration described in words, the Harbour paper header. Order for the reader: residue (tarballs public from 24 February, unread), propagation (Fedora and Debian builds), activity (Fedora's valgrind reports, then Freund's post); ends with which layer carried the first detected signal, who could see each, and the missing watch on distribution pipelines and on tarball versus Git. Kept the study's qualifications; used the narrower of two conflicting study statements on how widely liblzma reaches sshd; dated only Freund's post since Fedora's notification date differs. Draft awaiting the keeper's release decision. Committed as 6a132e7.

E-0001 Edit LH003 into an article. Draft, from studies/LH003/, the article that answers for a reader what we can actually see of AI activity on the internet: what repository activity, model usage reports and crawler measurements each expose, where their populations overlap or differ, and what remains invisible, without pretending the measurements add up to a census. Five minutes to read. Lead with the strongest supported finding and why it matters; keep the qualifications that change its meaning; remove the procedural clutter; name every source as the supplier of its evidence; describe one illustration in words if none can be drawn. Write it to articles/what-we-can-see.md as a draft. Done when the draft exists; release is the keeper's decision under LH F03. This will let us explain what the existing observatories reveal.

Work in the repository at /home/user/lighthouse. Follow AGENTS.md there. Commit the deliverable. When finished, report what you did, what could not be done, and the files you changed.
items.issueTitle: E-0001 Edit LH003 into an article

feedback.message: Drafted articles/what-we-can-see.md from LH003: about 1,200 words, three headings, one illustration described in words, the Harbour paper header. Leads with the finding that each of the seventeen sources covers one population in its own units and none states its overlap, so their numbers do not add to a total; labelled interpretation, with the two qualifications kept (no joint sample, documentation not tested against data). Sources reached only through search summaries left out and the article says so. Draft awaiting the keeper's release decision. Committed as 51752a3.
